UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE
FOREST SERVICE
857 WEST SOUTH JORDAN PARKWAY
SOUTH JORDAN, UTAH 84095

SPECIAL ORDER OF FOREST SUPERVISOR
UINTA-WASATCH-CACHE NATIONAL FOREST
OGDEN RANGER DISTRICT

PROHIBITIONS:

Pursuant to Title 36 CFR 261.50 (a) and (b) the following act is prohibited on the National Forest System Lands as described in this order. The area affected in this Order is located within the Ogden Ranger District, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. This order is in effect June 1st through November 15, 2018 annually.

  1. Building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire, campfire, or stove fire of any kind, including open flame, smoldering, or fueled by any other heat source used for personal warmth, lighting, ceremonial, esthetic purposes, or other, from June 1st through November 15th annually, as described below and shown on attached map. [36 CFR 261.52 (a)]

EXEMPTIONS:

Pursuant to 36 CFR 261.50 (e) the following persons are exempt from this order:

  1. Persons with special use authorization or other Forest Service authorization specifically exempting them from the effect of this Order.
  2. Any Federal, State, or local officer, or member of an organized rescue or fire fighting force in the performance of any official duty.
  3. Federal or State administrative personnel in performance of an official duty.

AREA DESCRIBED:

All National Forest System Lands located along the Wasatch Front foothills within Weber County that are on or below the 5,200 foot elevation or within 1/2 mile of any stucture on the east bench in Weber County located in Township 4 North, Range 1 West, Section 1; Township 5 North, Range 1 West, Sections 2, 11, 14 and 24; Township 6 North, Range 1 West, Section 10, 14, 23, 26, and 35; Township 7 North, Range 1 West, Sections 22, 23, 26, 34, and 35; Township 8 North, Range 2 West, Section 36 all within the Salt Lake Base Meridian as shown on the attached map.

PURPOSE:

Purpose of the closure is to reduce the Wildfire Risk in the foothills along the Wasatch Front in Weber and Box Elder County which is primarily high to extreme based on the State of Utah's Wildfire Risk Assessment Portal (UWRAP) data. The Wildfire Risk represents the possibility of loss or harm occurring from a wildfire and combines the likelihood of a fire occurring (Threat) with those areas of most concern that are adversely impacted by fire (Fire Effects). The High to Extreme Risk rating in ths area is driven by: 1) the proximity to the wildland urban interface, 2) a high probability of fire occurrence, 3) suppression difficulty due to steep terrain and a mix of flashy fuels and shrubs (primarily cheat grass and gambel oak), and 4) a high potential to negatively impact drinking water.

IMPLEMENTATION:

  1. This Order will be in effect when signed June 1st, and shall remain in effect through November 15th annually or until rescinded.
  2. Attached map shows the areas affected by this Order.
  3. Violation of the above prohibition(s) is punishable by a fine of not more than $5,000 for an individual or $10,000 for an organization and/or imprisonment for not more than 6 months imprisonment. [Title 16 USC 551, Title 18 USC 3571(b)(6), Title 18 USC 3581(b)(7)].
  4. Further information regarding this Order may be obtained at the Ogden Ranger District Office (801) 625-5112 or the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest Supervisors Office, Salt Lake City, Utah (801) 236-3400.
  5. This Order supersedes any previous Order(s) prohibiting the same, or similar acts prohibited by this Order in the areas (and/or roads or trails) covered by this Order.

Done at Salt Lake City, Utah this 3rd day of July, 2018.


David C. Whittekiend
Forest Supervisor

Order Number: 04-19-362

For more information regarding this closure order, please visit https://www.fs.usda.gov/uwcnf

UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE
FOREST SERVICE
8230 FEDERAL BUILDING, 125 SOUTH STATE STREET
SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH 84138
 

 

 

DAVIS COUNTY FIRE RESTRICTION
SPECIAL ORDER OF FOREST SUPERVISOR
WASATCH-CACHE NATIONAL FOREST
SALT LAKE RANGER DISTRICT

 

The purpose of this order is to protect public health, well-being and safety.

Pursuant to 36 CFR 261.50 (a) and (b), in addition to the General Prohibitions, the following acts are prohibited on the area described below and as shown on the attached map. All lands affected are located on the Salt Lake Ranger District, Wasatch-Cache National Forest. This order is in effect until further notice

  1. Building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire, campfire, or stove fire of any kind, including open flame, smoldering, or fuels by any other heat source used for cooking, personal warmth, lighting, ceremonial, esthetic purposes, or other, from April 1 through October 31 annually. [36 CFR 261.52 (a)]

Pursuant to 36 CFR 216.50 (e), the following acts, or persons, are exempt from this order:

  1. Persons with a permit or contract authorizing the otherwise prohibited act, issued by the District Ranger for a specified period/location
  2. Authorized Federal, State, or local officers, or active members of an organized rescue or firefighting force when necessary in the performance of official duty.
  3. Persons using portable gas stoves, lanterns, or tent heaters which use gas, gellied petroleum, or pressurized liquid fuel either outdoors or within a building, mobile home, an enclosed recreational vehicle, or tent, unless otherwise posted as closed to such use.
  4. Building, maintaining, attending or using a fire, campfire, or stove fire within a permanent facility constructed by and/or administered by the USDA Forest Service within open developed campgrounds, picnic areas, or administrative sites, unless otherwise posted as closed to such use.

Area Described: All National Forest System lands located along the Wasatch Front foothills within Davis County that are on or below the 5,200 foot elevation (the approximate "high water" mark or "bench" of the old Lake Bonneville Shoreline), or within 1/2 mile of any residential structure on or east of that bench, between the Davis/Weber County line and the Davis/Salt Lake County line, as shown on the attached map.

Bernie Weingardt
Forest Supervisor
Wasatch-Cache National Forest

June 20, 2000

Violation of this prohibition is punishable by fine of not more than $5,000 or imprisonment of not more than 6 months or both (16 USC 551; 18 USC 3571 (b) (6)).

Order Number 04 (Region) 19 (Forest) 109 (Numeric Sequence)
